Saudi Ministry of Media/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY. OVERLAY FROM SOURCE. VERIFICATION: Reuters verified the location from the CCTV of the boarding gate from the infrastructure and furniture that matched the archive and satellite imagery from terminal 3 at King Khalid International Airport. The date the video was filmed was confirmed with the timestamp on the surveillance footage. The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said the airport operations were suspended after an attack that left many injured on October 10. No old results were found posted online before October 11.

Ateeq Shariff | Reuters News

Most Gulf stock markets ended lower on Sunday, as geopolitical concerns weighed on sentiment after an attack on Riyadh's international airport left at least 12 dead and more than 300 wounded, marking the kingdom's deadliest attack in over a decade. 

Adding to the uncertainty, Yemen's Houthis on Sunday warned airlines, travellers and airport workers to stay away from Saudi airports. 

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index narrowed early losses to finish 0.2% lower with the country's biggest lender by assets Saudi National Bank losing 1.1%. Oil major Saudi Aramco was down 0.2%.

 President Donald Trump has said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis, widening a regional conflict that spilled over from the US-Israeli war with Iran. 

Riyadh and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes against targets in Houthi-held territory in Yemen. The Houthis have said these killed civilians including women and children. 

Reuters could not independently verify those claims.

In Qatar, the benchmark index declined 1.5%, falling for a fourth consecutive session and closing at its lowest since May 2020, with Qatar Islamic Bank declining 1.7%. 

Geopolitical risks continue to weigh on sentiment, with stalled US-Iran talks constraining risk appetite and reports of renewed escalation adding to caution. 

Concerns are likely to remain elevated as tanker attacks and maritime disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz persist, said Milad Azar, market analyst at XTB MENA.

 Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index - which traded after a session's break — declined 2%, with all its constituents closing in negative territory including Commercial International Bank , which was down 1.6%. 

Saudi Arabia lost 0.2% to 10,361 Qatar dropped 1.5% to 8,875 Egypt declined 2% to 52,207 Bahrain fell 0.3% to 1,890 Oman added 0.3% to 7,842 Kuwait inched 0.1% higher to 9,037

(Reporting by Ateeq Shariff in Bengaluru; Editing by Elaine Hardcastle, Alexandra Hudson)
